To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We have identified novel TRAIL sensitizers that promote apoptosis of tumor cells in a synergistic manner; (2) We have identified a subset of these TRAIL sensitizing compounds as rapid caspase- 8 activators; and (3) We have identified two TRAIL sensitizing agents that induce DNA damage, but are not proteasome inhibitors.

we have developed a cell-based high-through-put screen to identify novel TRAIL sensitizers, and have found that some of the sensitizers act very quickly to promote caspase- 8 cleavage and activation, suggesting that these sensitizers may be useful in reducing tumor resistance to TRAIL- mediated apoptosis.
we have developed a cell-based high-throughout screen (HTS), using a 384-well format, to identify novel TRAIL sensitizers that synergize with TRail to promote tumor cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a cell-based high-through-put screening assay to identify novel TRAIL sensitizers that can promote tumor cell apoptosis.
the identification of new compounds and pure natural extracts that can synergize the pro-apoptotic effects of TRAIL.
the discovery of new small molecules that sensitize tumor cells to TRail-mediated apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HTS is a useful tool for discovering novel sensitizers of TRAIL-induced apoptosis.
